question: The Consular Digitalisation Plan of the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation has been granted EUR 115 million in NextGenerationEU funds under component 11 of Spain’s Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan (RTRP). The ministry has linked the digitalisation in question to its capacity to process applications for citizenship under what is known as the grandchildren’s law1.

In addition, the Border Management and Visa Instrument (BMVI) provides EUR 30 million in EU funding to support consular offices and Schengen visa points. At the same time, the Spanish consulate in Havana has concluded a contract worth EUR 1 131 295.

68 (plus VAT) with Palco, a Cuban state-owned company, subcontracting it to provide between 88 and 107 workers who, according to press reports, could access sensitive personal data relating to those applying for Spanish nationality under the grandchildren’s law. In view of the above: 1.
Can the Commission confirm whether the reinforcement of the consulate staff by Cuban company Palco is funded, directly or indirectly, under component 11 of the RTRP or under the BMVI?
Has Spain established before the Commission that the NextGenerationEU funds linked to consular digitalisation do not pay for functions carried out by the staff of a non-EU state entity?
If EU funds have been earmarked for this contract, what action does the Commission intend to take?
